title: Liszt, Hungarian Rhapsody No. 2: three recordings
work: Hungarian Rhapsody No. 2, S. 244/2 — shared opening
question: What happens to Liszt’s pauses and flourishes when the piano writing is arranged for orchestra?
intro: Liszt opens with accented chords, pauses and quick flourishes. Rachmaninoff plays the piano original; Stokowski’s Philadelphia players use Karl Müller-Berghaus’s orchestration. Goehr adds a London performance from Kingsway Hall. In all three recordings this opening begins the first disc side.

recordings.label: Sergei Rachmaninoff, 1919
recordings.note: Rachmaninoff plays Liszt’s solo original for Edison, in his first year of gramophone recording.

recordings.label: Leopold Stokowski, Philadelphia Orchestra, 1936
recordings.note: The Philadelphia Orchestra plays Karl Müller-Berghaus’s orchestration, which arranges Liszt’s piano writing for orchestra.

recordings.label: Walter Goehr, National Symphony Orchestra of London, 1945
recordings.note: Goehr recorded the National Symphony Orchestra of London at Kingsway Hall in 1945.

passages.label: Opening with accented chords
passages.note: Accented chords punctuate a winding line; short flourishes run between the broad notes.

passages.label: Slow melody over repeated bass
passages.note: The slow melody is played above a repeated bass figure, with short turns placed between its longer notes.

passages.label: Melody in chords
passages.note: The melody is filled out in chords, while the bass keeps its heavy tread.

sources.title: Goehr — Kingsway Hall, 1945, first side; the source does not identify an arranger
